Package com.epitech.depthdiablo.engine

Class StateBuffer

java.lang.Object
com.epitech.depthdiablo.engine.StateBuffer
public final class StateBuffer extends Object
One photo of the game for the R rewind (GDD 1.1.2, Q86): every Rewindable writes its values here one after another, then reads them back in the same order to go back to that moment. The buffer does not know what a value means, only its place, so readState must read exactly what writeState wrote, in the same order.

Values live in primitive arrays, one per type, so recording 60 photos per second creates no boxed numbers and no garbage (Q86). The arrays double when they are full and are kept by clear(), so a reused photo stops allocating once it is big enough.

Pattern: Memento, the stored state (Rewindable is the originator, Rewind the caretaker).

  • Method Details

    • clear

      public void clear()
      Forgets everything written and keeps the arrays, so the next photo in this buffer allocates nothing. The references are dropped too, so a dead entity is no longer held here.

    • readRef

      public <T> T readRef(Class<T> type)
      Reads the next reference, in the order they were written.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type the caller expects
      Parameters:
      type - the class the caller expects, e.g. Character.class
      Returns:
      the same object that was written, or null if null was written
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if type is null
      IllegalStateException - if every written reference was already read
      ClassCastException - if the object is not of the given type
